subject: surgery
title: Vesicoureteric Reflux, Wilms Tumour and Neuroblastoma

steps.tx: Imaging the bladder and urethra while the child voids contrast is a **voiding cystourethrogram**. It shows reflux into ureters and outlines the posterior urethra. It is the key test after urinary infection with abnormal ultrasound in young children. Grade one reflux reaches the ureter only, grade three dilates it mildly, and grade five twists a grossly dilated ureter.
steps.say: A voiding cystourethrogram images voiding to show reflux and the posterior urethra.

steps.tx: Backward flow of urine from bladder to ureter and kidney is graded as **vesicoureteric reflux grading**. Grades run from reflux into ureter only up to grossly dilated tortuous systems. Higher grades scar kidneys more and resolve less often spontaneously. Most grade one and two reflux resolves as the child grows, at roughly 10 to 15 percent per year in early childhood.
steps.say: Vesicoureteric reflux grading runs from ureter only to grossly dilated systems with scarring.

steps.tx: The commonest malignant kidney tumour of childhood is the **Wilms tumour**. Also called nephroblastoma, it usually presents as a painless abdominal mass in a three year old. Most are found by parents while bathing the child. Unlike neuroblastoma, a Wilms tumour rarely crosses the midline and seldom calcifies on imaging, two separators worth stating.
steps.say: Wilms tumour, or nephroblastoma, presents as a painless abdominal mass in young children.

vis.alt: Wilms tumour within paediatric urological conditions.
vis.caption: Wilms tumour assessment. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Embryonal kidney tissue forming a triphasic tumour defines **nephroblastoma** histology. Blastemal, epithelial and stromal elements mix together. Favourable histology without anaplasia carries an excellent prognosis with modern therapy. Anaplasia in the tumour worsens outlook sharply and pushes treatment toward stronger chemotherapy and radiotherapy.
steps.say: Nephroblastoma mixes three tissue types, and absence of anaplasia predicts excellent prognosis.

steps.tx: A tumour of sympathetic nerve tissue, often in the adrenal gland, is **neuroblastoma**. It is the commonest solid tumour of infancy outside the brain. Spread to bone and orbit causes periorbital bruising in advanced cases. Opsoclonus myoclonus, dancing eyes and jerky movements, is the paraneoplastic syndrome linked to neuroblastoma in toddlers.
steps.say: Neuroblastoma arises from sympathetic tissue, often adrenal, and spreads to bone and orbit.

vis.alt: Neuroblastoma: abdominal tumour encasing the aorta with orbital spread.
vis.caption: Neuroblastoma: abdominal tumour encasing the aorta with orbital spread. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Gentle palpation only is the rule for a suspected Wilms mass, called **no vigorous palpation**. Rough handling can rupture the tumour and worsen staging. Cross sectional imaging precedes any operative intervention. Biopsy before chemotherapy is avoided in typical Wilms tumour because spilling cells upstages the child.
steps.say: Suspected Wilms masses need gentle palpation only because rupture worsens staging.

steps.tx: Chemotherapy before surgery shrinks large Wilms tumours in many protocols, called **neoadjuvant treatment**. It reduces rupture risk at operation. Staging after resection then guides further therapy intensity. Preoperative chemotherapy over four weeks shrinks most tumours and cuts the rupture rate at surgery to under 5 percent in trials.
steps.say: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy shrinks large Wilms tumours and reduces rupture risk at surgery.

steps.tx: Syndromes predisposing to Wilms tumour include WAGR and Beckwith-Wiedemann, grouped as **predisposition syndromes**. Affected children receive regular ultrasound screening of the kidneys. Screening finds tumours while they are small and curable. Screening scans run every three months until age seven for Beckwith-Wiedemann children, the group at highest risk.
steps.say: Predisposition syndromes like WAGR receive regular kidney ultrasound screening for early Wilms detection.

steps.tx: Urine infection prevention in high grade reflux may use low dose nightly antibiotics, termed **antibiotic prophylaxis**. Breakthrough infections or new scars push toward surgical correction of reflux. Many low grades resolve as the bladder grows. Dexell or bulking injection at the ureter opening offers a lower morbidity fix for persistent middle grade reflux.
steps.say: Antibiotic prophylaxis protects high grade reflux, while low grades often resolve with growth.
